problem_type: agent worktree and dependency lifecycle leak
symptom: Nomi accumulates stopped worktrees and repeated node_modules trees, consuming disk space after agent tasks finish.
direct_cause: Worktree creation and dependency installation have an enforced start path, but task stop has no shared lease marker or safe reclaim path; the existing Stop hook checks delivery evidence only.
class_root: Agent task lifecycle has no shared stop boundary that records ownership and separates rebuildable dependencies from user code and branch state.
affected_population: Any future agent task that installs dependencies in an isolated Nomi checkout
entry_points: Claude Stop hook invoking scripts/agent-worktree-janitor.mjs stop
internal_only_reason: This change enforces an internal repository and local-agent lifecycle invariant; no third-party API contract decides whether a worktree's code or dependencies are disposable.
invariants: Only a stopped, inactive, grace-period-expired worktree may be reclaimed.
Dirty or detached code is never removed automatically.
Full clones are never removed automatically; only rebuildable dependency directories may be pruned.
Unmanaged worktrees without a stop marker are left untouched.
generality_proof: All supported agent checkouts converge on the repository-provided Stop hook and janitor policy. The policy classifies linked worktrees, detached worktrees, and full clones before any filesystem mutation, so equivalent task endings cannot bypass the code-versus-dependency safety boundary.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Record the stopped lease, check activity and grace period, and select only safe dependency pruning or linked-worktree removal.
Install one idempotent repository-relative Stop hook on a developer machine without embedding a machine-specific checkout path.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: The stop command writes the lease marker before reaping the repository's registered worktrees and sibling full clones.
The reap command uses the same decision policy for explicit/manual cleanup, so it cannot bypass active, grace, dirty, detached, or full-clone protections.
The installer is the shared setup path for Claude Stop integration and emits a repository-relative command that works in each checkout.

recurrence.reason: Every parallel agent run can create the same disposable dependency tree, and the existing stop path has no cleanup ownership or expiry signal.
same_class_scan: CLAUDE.md worktree and pnpm install rules: independent worktrees are created repeatedly without a disposal step.
docs/engineering/agent-orchestration-playbook.md lifecycle guidance: liveness is judged but no repository cleanup callback is enforced.
scripts/agent-worktree-janitor.mjs stop and reap: both converge on the new policy boundary.

prevention.invariant: No worktree is removed or dependency directory is pruned unless it has a stopped lease, has passed the grace period, and is not active; code and full-clone boundaries remain protected.
prevention.failure_mode: Missing, malformed, fresh, active, dirty-code, detached, or full-clone state fails closed to skip or dependency-only pruning.
prevention.strategy: Make stop ownership explicit, then reuse one classifier for automatic Stop-hook cleanup and manual reap so equivalent entry points cannot invent different deletion rules.

legacy_paths.rationale: The existing machine-local hook remains a local installation detail; this change adds the versioned repository implementation and installer without removing unrelated project hooks.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: The invariant is implemented with Node.js standard-library and Git/lsof commands already required by the local workflow; no third-party runtime controls the lifecycle decision.

migration: Developers run pnpm run install:agent-worktree-janitor once per checkout. Existing unmanaged worktrees are not retroactively deleted; only future stops create leases, preserving unknown user work.
residual_risks: Codex does not expose a repository task-stop callback in this environment, so full clones require the shared installer or an explicit reap invocation to create/use a lease; the janitor still never deletes their code.
